# 1 Enoch Chapter 98 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch — Woe Oracles

---

**98:1** Now I swear to you, the wise and the foolish alike, that you will see many things on the earth.

**98:2** For you men shall put on more adornments than a woman, and more colorful garments than a virgin: in royalty and grandeur and power, and in silver and gold and purple, and in splendor and food shall you be lavished like water.

**98:3** Therefore you shall lack doctrine and wisdom, and shall perish together with your possessions; and with all your glory and splendor, in shame and slaughter and great destitution, your spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

**98:4** I have sworn to you, sinners: as a mountain has not become a slave, and a hill does not become the handmaid of a woman, even so sin was not sent upon the earth — but man created it himself — and under a great curse shall they fall who commit it.

**98:5** And barrenness was not given to the woman, but on account of the deeds of her own hands she dies without children.

**98:6** I swear to you, sinners, by the Holy and Great One, that all your evil deeds are revealed in the heavens, and that none of your deeds of oppression are covered or hidden.

**98:7** Do not think in your spirit, nor say in your heart, that you do not know and do not see that every sin is recorded every day in heaven in the presence of the Most High.

**98:8** From henceforth know that all your oppression, with which you oppress, is written down every day until the day of your judgment.

**98:9** Woe to you, fools, for through your folly you shall perish; you transgress against the wise, and so good fortune shall not be your portion.

**98:10** And now know that you are prepared for the day of destruction; therefore do not hope to live, sinners, but you shall depart and die; for you know no ransom; for you are prepared for the day of the great judgment, for the day of tribulation and great shame for your spirits.

**98:11** Woe to you, you stubborn of heart, who work wickedness and eat blood: from what source do you have good things to eat and to drink and to be filled? From all the good things which the Lord Most High has placed in abundance on the earth; therefore you shall have no peace.

**98:12** Woe to you who love the deeds of unrighteousness: why do you hope for good fortune for yourselves? Know that you shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous, and they shall cut off your necks and slay you, and shall have no mercy upon you.

**98:13** Woe to you who rejoice at the trouble of the righteous, for no grave shall be dug for you.

**98:14** Woe to those who set at nothing the words of the upright, for you shall have no hope of life.

**98:15** Woe to those who write down lying and godless words, for they write their lies that men may hear them and act godlessly toward their neighbor.

**98:16** Therefore they shall have no peace but shall die a swift death.

---

*SOPHIA notes: LOGOS register adopted throughout. V. 4 — the declaration that sin is a human creation, not a divine ordinance — is the theological climax of the chapter and preserved in strict formal rendering. The mountain/hill analogy is not allegorical window dressing; it is a carefully constructed negative proof. V. 7's heavenly record motif anticipates the great cosmic ledger of ch. 104. 'Good fortune' (vv. 9, 12) preferred over EMET's 'good hap' (archaic). Divergences logged.*
